questions.prompt: What problem do separate ResourceDictionary files solve in a growing WPF app?
options: They let WinForms forms reuse the app's WPF styles and brushes
They make every `StaticResource` lookup update at runtime
They let you split resources out of App.xaml into separate files
They replace the need to write styles and templates at all
questions.explanation: Without ResourceDictionary files everything goes into App.xaml, which becomes huge, hard to manage and difficult to reuse; dictionaries let you split resources into separate files.

questions.prompt: You create `Resources/Colors.xaml` containing `PrimaryBrush`, but `{StaticResource PrimaryBrush}` cannot be found anywhere in the app. What is the likely mistake?
options: Colors.xaml was never merged into App.xaml's `MergedDictionaries`
Brushes cannot be stored in a separate ResourceDictionary file
`PrimaryBrush` must be referenced with `TemplateBinding` instead
A ResourceDictionary file must always be named `App.xaml`
questions.explanation: A dictionary file is only used once it is merged, typically through `<ResourceDictionary.MergedDictionaries>` in `Application.Resources`. "Forgetting to merge dictionary" is one of the lesson's common mistakes.

questions.prompt: Who decides how much space a WPF control gets?
options: The control itself, from its `Width` and `Height`
The Window, which gives every control the same size
The ViewModel bound to the control
The parent decides, and the child adapts
questions.explanation: In WPF the viewport is the space a control is given by its parent: a control does not decide its size; the parent decides and the child adapts.

questions.prompt: You want a 30% / 70% two-column layout that keeps those proportions when the window is resized. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Bind each column's `Width` to `ActualWidth` of the root grid multiplied by 0.3 and 0.7
Use `<ColumnDefinition Width="30*"/>` and `<ColumnDefinition Width="70*"/>`
Position the two areas on a Canvas and recalculate in code-behind on resize
Use `Width="30%"` and `Width="70%"`
questions.explanation: WPF has no % sizing; Grid star sizing is its percentage equivalent, so `30*` and `70*` give 30% / 70%. Binding to `ActualWidth` or calculating in code-behind breaks the layout passes.

questions.prompt: A Grid has three columns: `Width="2*"`, `Width="3*"` and `Width="5*"`. How is the width shared?
options: 2px / 3px / 5px
The third column takes everything left after the first two size to content
questions.explanation: Star values are parts of the remaining space: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 parts, so the columns get 20%, 30% and 50%.

questions.prompt: According to the responsive-UI rules, where is a `Viewbox` appropriate?
options: Around vector visuals such as logos and icons
Around data entry forms, so they scale to any window
Around DataGrids, so all columns always fit
Around the whole main window, in place of Grid star sizing
questions.explanation: Rule 5 says to use Viewbox only for vector visuals like logos and icons, not for forms or data grids, since it scales the whole subtree and text may blur if overused.
